propositions: Mutation testing subprocess execution (mutmut run and baseline pytest in execute_shard) must be sandboxed to deny destructive file operations outside an explicit allow-list, preventing mutants that remove guards from shell scripts from executing commands like rm -rf /

The sandbox must be OS-enforced (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux) and fail-closed; without a mechanism available on a workstation the gate aborts with a message naming REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED, while CI runners may proceed with a WARNING

Sandbox enforcement must be empirically observed by test: a probe writing outside the allow-list must exit non-zero with the file absent afterward, and the incident's specific shape (rm -rf <protected>/*) must be demonstrably denied

HOME must be set to a non-existent path for sandboxed subprocesses so adjacent home-directory writes fail, verified by running children and observing their actual HOME rather than asserting only on the returned mapping

Linux bwrap enforcement must be proven on Linux (ubuntu:24.04 container measured: write outside DENIED, write inside succeeded, rm -rf <protected>/* DENIED) rather than inferred from macOS, with explicit tracking of CI runner gaps where unprivileged user namespaces are disabled
The venv (sys.prefix) is deliberately excluded from the sandbox allow-list to prevent mutants from dropping executable code into site-packages for later un-sandboxed phases to import
